ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON THE ESTABLISHMENT AND OPERATION OF THE NATIONAL FIRE HOSPITAL

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Act on the Establishment and Operation of the National Fire Hospital and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 2 (Persons Eligible for Medical Treatment, etc.)
(1) The National Fire Hospital (hereinafter referred to as the "Fire Hospital") shall provide medical treatment to the following persons pursuant to Article 5 (1) of the Act on the Establishment and Operation of the National Fire Hospital (hereinafter referred to as the "Act"):
1. Fire officials under the Fire Officials Act (hereinafter referred to as "fire officials");
2. Obligatory fire service personnel appointed pursuant to Article 3 of the Act on the Establishment of an Obligatory Fire Service;
3. Persons injured while undergoing education or training at a fire service education and training institution established pursuant to Article 20 of the Fire Officials Act (including occupational diseases; hereinafter the same shall apply in this Article);
4. Members of volunteer fire brigades under the Act on the Establishment and Operation of Volunteer Fire Brigades;
5. Public officials serving at fire service agencies as defined in subparagraph 3 of Article 2 of the Decree on the Appointment of Fire Officials;
6. Police officials under the Police Officials Act (including autonomous police officials under the Special Act on the Establishment of Jeju Special Self-Governing Province and the Development of Free International City; hereinafter referred to as "police officials");
7. Persons injured while undergoing education or training at a police education and training institution established pursuant to Article 22 of the Police Officials Act;
8. Public officials serving at the Korean National Police Agency and its affiliated agencies under the Organization of the Korean National Police Agency and Its Affiliated Agencies;
9. Public officials serving at the Korea Coast Guard and its affiliated agencies under the Organization of the Korea Coast Guard and Its Affiliated Agencies;
10. Spouses and lineal ascendants and descendants among the family members of fire officials or police officials;
11. Persons who have retired after serving as fire officials or police officials for at least 20 years;
12. Other persons who need to receive medical treatment for the performance of the activities prescribed in Article 5 (1) 2 through 10 of the Act.
(2) Where the Fire Hospital provides medical treatment to persons referred to in paragraph (1), it may reduce or exempt the portion of the medical treatment expenses payable by those persons.
(3) Detailed matters necessary for reductions or exemptions under paragraph (2) shall be determined by the President with the approval of the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency.

Article 3 (Duties and Remuneration of Persons Holding Concurrent Positions)
(1) A person who concurrently performs duties at the Fire Hospital pursuant to Article 8 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "person holding a concurrent position") shall comply with the articles of incorporation and various regulations of the Fire Hospital and faithfully perform the research and medical treatment duties of the Fire Hospital.
(2) The Fire Hospital may bear all or part of the remuneration of persons holding concurrent positions and other expenses associated with such concurrent positions.

Article 4 (Release from Concurrent Positions)
Where a person holding a concurrent position violates Article 3 (1), or where a person holding a concurrent position who is an educational public official falls under any subparagraph of Article 78 (1) of the State Public Officials Act, the President may, following deliberation by the personnel committee prescribed by the articles of incorporation, request the head of the university, research institution, or medical institution to which such person belongs to take appropriate measures, such as releasing the person from the concurrent position.

Article 5 (Requests for Contributions and Applications for Payment)
(1) Where the Fire Hospital submits a request for a budget for contributions for the following business year under Article 13 (2) of the Act, it shall attach the following documents:
1. A business plan for the following business year;
2. A projected statement of financial position and a projected income statement for the following business year;
3. Other documents necessary to clearly explain the details of the request for a budget for contributions.
(2) To receive payment of contributions, the Fire Hospital shall submit an application for payment of contributions to the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency, accompanied by a quarterly budget execution plan.

Article 6 (Free Lease of State Property)
The particulars, conditions, procedures, and other matters concerning a free lease of State property under Article 14 (1) of the Act shall be governed by a contract between the management authority for the relevant State property and the Fire Hospital.

Article 7 (Submission of Business Plans, etc.)
(1) Where the Fire Hospital prepares and submits a business plan under Article 16 (1) of the Act, it shall separately state the objectives, policies, main details, and necessary budget for its business activities.
(2) "Important matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 16 (2) of the Act means the following matters:
1. The establishment or discontinuance of a business activity;
2. A budget change exceeding 10 percent of the total budget.

Article 8 (Submission of Statements of Settlement of Accounts)
Where the Fire Hospital submits a statement of settlement of revenues and expenditures to the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency under Article 17 of the Act, it shall attach the following documents:
1. A statement of financial position and an income statement for the relevant year;
2. A table comparing the business plan for the relevant year with the actual results of its implementation;
3. An audit report prepared by the auditor and a financial audit report prepared by a certified public accountant;
4. Other supporting documents by which the details of the settlement of accounts may be confirmed.

Article 9 (Treatment of Surplus)
Where a surplus arises as a result of the settlement of accounts for each business year, the Fire Hospital shall apply the surplus to making up losses carried forward and carry the remainder forward to the following business year.

Article 10 (Methods of Entrusting Management and Operation, etc.)
(1) Where the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency intends to select a corporation to be entrusted with the management and operation of the Fire Hospital pursuant to Article 19 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an "entrusted entity"), the Commissioner shall invite applications through an open call and shall disclose the criteria for selecting the entrusted entity, the allocation of evaluation points, etc. in the announcement of the open call.
(2) The Commissioner of the National Fire Agency shall select an eligible entity following an evaluation by the Deliberation Committee on Eligible Entrusted Entities composed of experts in the relevant field, and shall publicly announce the selection on the website of the National Fire Agency, etc.
(3) Where the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency concludes an entrustment contract with an entrusted entity pursuant to Article 19 (3) of the Act, the Commissioner shall publicly notify the name of the entrusted entity, the details of the entrusted affairs, the period of entrustment, etc.
(4) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (3), detailed matters necessary for the composition of the Deliberation Committee on Eligible Entrusted Entities, the methods of selecting entrusted entities, the conclusion of contracts, etc. shall be prescribed by the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency.

Article 11 (Methods of Conducting Operational Evaluations, etc.)
(1) The Commissioner of the National Fire Agency shall annually conduct an operational evaluation of the Fire Hospital under Article 20 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an "operational evaluation").
(2) The detailed criteria for operational evaluations shall be as follows:
1. The profitability and public-service role of the Fire Hospital shall be evaluated separately;
2. The following indicators shall be evaluated:
(a) Evaluation of the management status of the Fire Hospital: Accountable management, financial self-reliance, hospital management, etc.;
(b) Evaluation of the performance of projects under Article 5 (1) of the Act and customer service: Contributions to society, the medical care environment, etc.
(3) The Commissioner of the National Fire Agency shall prepare evaluation guidelines specifying the basic direction, criteria, subjects, schedule, etc. of operational evaluations and notify the President thereof at least 90 days before the scheduled date of an operational evaluation.

Article 12 (Secondment of Public Officials)
(1) Where the Fire Hospital requests the head of a relevant administrative agency to second public officials under the head's jurisdiction pursuant to Article 21 of the Act, it shall specify the specialized fields and qualification requirements of the public officials to be seconded, the positions to be assigned to them, the duties to be performed by them, etc.
(2) The Fire Hospital may pay duty allowances to public officials seconded pursuant to paragraph (1), as prescribed by its articles of incorporation.

Article 13 (Processing of Unique Identifying Information)
Where it is unavoidable for performing affairs relating to verification of grounds for disqualification of officers under Article 7 of the Act, the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency may process data containing resident registration numbers under subparagraph 1 of Article 19 of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act.

Article 14 (Criteria for Imposing Administrative Fines)

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 31885, July 13, 2021>

This Decree shall enter into force on July 13, 2021.
